notes: r5 (2026-10-19): far less stutter in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024. The stutter was the game's main thread translating code again after the game's copy protection rewrote it, about 220 page invalidations a second in the memory that also holds the game's own code. FEX patch 0023 adds switches the game's recipe turns on: a store that writes back the bytes already in memory no longer throws the page's translations away (a third of those writes), code on a page the protection just wrote is translated in small units for a few seconds (multiblock translated about four times what runs there), translations whose bytes come back are reinstated (FEX 0020), and FEX's global locks are out of the paths that do not need them. On a base M4 at Gibraltar in daylight (Medium, FSR Balanced, 1920x931 windowed), against r4 with the same recipe otherwise: frames over 100 ms fell from 59 to 5 per 2-minute park and from 55 to 23 per minute of take-off roll, frames over 250 ms from 9 to 0.5 and from 7.5 to 2.2, the 99th percentile frame time from 160 to 71 ms parked and from 220 to 122 ms rolling, and the frame rate rose from 19 to 22.5 parked and from 16 to 19 rolling (four flights against two, three windows of each kind a flight; p < 0.001 parked and rolling).

Also since r3: an unhandled exception in an x86-64 program logs its full register state (patches-arm64 0041), RtlIsEcCode answers FALSE above the user address space instead of faulting until the stack runs out (0042), and a program sees the page protection it set rather than FEX's write trap (FEX 0022, Wine 0043). Wine 11.18 with patches-arm64 0001 to 0043, FEX 2610 with fex/patches 0001 to 0023; MoltenVK and the renderers are r3's. Every 0023 switch is off unless a recipe sets it: other games run as on r4.

Known: about one boot in sixteen to forty ends in a crash during the world load (a thread resumes with a wrong stack pointer; under study); a half-second GPU stall on the terrain pass, zero to two a flight; the launch takes about seven minutes to the start screen and four more to the cockpit on warm caches; lights drawn as point sprites and some line effects are missing (Metal has no geometry shaders); far map tiles on the Free Flight page stay coarse; motion blur is best off. A 16 GB Mac is unlikely to hold the game's 25 GB footprint.

Environments on this engine are new ones: an environment never moves between an Intel engine and this line. The engine's renderers are the vkd3d and dxvk folders of the renderers component, loaded through WINEDLLPATH as on the Intel line.

verified.result: Steam copy of Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 on a Mac mini M4 with 32 GB through Highball's test harness, the recipe's FEX switches on: boot, Free Flight, a Cessna 172 at Gibraltar, three 2-minute parks and three 1-minute take-off rolls with two in-game restarts a flight, in daylight. Flights hunt104 (FEX DLL built on the M4 from the same source), hunt107, hunt110 and hunt111 (this archive): no crash, no unhandled exception, no GPU hang (hunt111 had two of the known half-second terrain-pass stalls, and it went on), about 7 minutes to the start screen and 13 to the cockpit; 5 frames over 100 ms per 2-minute park (r4: 59), 22.5 fps parked and 19 rolling (r4: 19 and 16). The x86-64 fidelity programs pass with the switches on, 64 and 32-bit. Not tested: camera turns, other aircraft or airports, a long session, other Macs.
